headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI can ingest shared workspace content while Airflow can egress broadly, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error exposure; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have no explicit direct message channel, but B reads shared workspace pages and A can interact with external content via broad network egress. The only plausible bridge is manual or workspace-mediated content transfer, so injection risk exists but is not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-generated text into a Notion page that B later summarizes or answers from, injection becomes plausible.
IF B is pointed at a page containing attacker-controlled instructions, B may follow them.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces or pages.
Strip instructions from A outputs before pasting into Notion.
Use a fixed prompt template for B that ignores embedded directives.
Review any A-generated content before it is stored in shared pages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read workspace pages and team knowledge base content by default, while A has broad network egress. Even though A does not expose filesystem access, the pair can move workspace content into externally reachable systems, so sensitive workspace data can leak beyond the intended boundary.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain sensitive internal material and A is used to process or export that material, leakage risk is present.
IF B is allowed to summarize pages that A later transmits to external services, the data leaves the workspace boundary.
mitigations: Restrict A to non-sensitive datasets.
Mark sensitive Notion pages as off-limits for AI workflows.
Disable or review any A workflow that exports page content externally.
Use a separate workspace for confidential material.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no filesystem write, git, or shell execution, and B explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell, and subprocess capabilities. The pair therefore has little direct write-write contention; only shared workspace content can be edited through Notion-controlled actions, which is a narrower conflict surface.
conditions: IF both agents are tasked with editing the same Notion page concurrently, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF an external orchestrator maps A outputs into B edits on the same resource, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole editor for each page.
Use sequential rather than parallel updates.
Add a manual review step before B writes changes.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same workspace object.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it can treat A-produced text as authoritative if that text is stored in pages B later reads. A can generate or transform content that B then summarizes or acts on, creating a default-path cascade unless the operator adds verification.
conditions: IF A-generated content is written into a Notion page that B uses as source material, B may propagate errors.
IF B is asked to draft decisions from A-produced summaries without verification, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require source links for any A-derived claim.
Have B cite original documents, not A summaries.
Insert a human verification step before B publishes outputs.
Limit B to retrieval, not decision-making, on A-derived pages.

E_compliance.rationale: B handles workspace pages and team knowledge base content under Notion workspace permissions, while A has broad network egress and no documented residency or retention controls. If regulated or region-bound content is processed by both, the pair can create a compliance mismatch even though only B has explicit workspace access.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated content is stored in Notion pages and A exports or processes it externally, residency/compliance obligations may be breached.
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter retention rules than the external service used by A, mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A workflows.
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings before use.
Tag compliance-sensitive pages and exclude them from AI access.
Use separate workspaces for regulated and non-regulated content.
